name: to_sparse_csr
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim: aten::to_sparse_csr(Tensor self, int? dense_dim=None) -> Tensor. This representative signature is not exclusive: the original Gems pytest owns the full contract for overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation, and no tests or reference semantics may be removed or adapted to fit this one signature. Registered ATen schema strings supplied as evidence (all of them): "aten::to_sparse_csr(Tensor self, int? dense_dim=None) -> Tensor". Semantics derived from the tests: converts a dense tensor into a 2-D sparse CSR tensor; dense_dim selects how many trailing axes become the dense tail (default 0, i.e. the last two axes are the sparse matrix and every leading axis is a batch axis), and the valid range is [0, rank - 2]; leading axes are batch axes and a batched conversion requires a non-zero batch product; only non-zero entries are stored, an all-zero input stores no elements, and zero-sized matrix or dense-tail extents remain valid; index tensors are int64 for a dense source and keep the source dtype for a compressed source; a dense input is never mutated, while the default call on an already-CSR source returns that same object (a conditional aliasing behavior that this single-overload model does not express); a BSR source and an explicit dense_dim on a CSR source are rejected; via autograd the dense upstream gradient is returned unchanged. Only the runner-visible contract for the representative overload is recorded here; scalar/list keyword forms, sparse-source conversion, alias-on-CSR, and every error class remain defined by the pytest.
